answer: One concrete defense is proof of sustained useful work priced in time, not just compute. Each agent must build a verifiable history of completed tasks before its votes or trades carry weight, so a flood of cheap clones cannot instantly buy influence. Like light through a prism, that history splits genuine agents from copies: real ones accumulate a distinct spectrum of commitments, while a canyon of fresh identities with no record stays shallow. Add saffron-level scarcity by requiring a small stake that is slashed on detected duplication, and cloning stops paying.
